59811-rainbow-bridge-national-monument-u.title: Rainbow Bridge National Monument Utah 1951
59811-rainbow-bridge-national-monument-u.creator: Unknown
59811-rainbow-bridge-national-monument-u.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. While leading an archeological expedition through southeastern Utah and northern Arizona during the summer of 1908, Dr. Byron Cummings, then Dean of Arts and Sciences, University of Utah, became interested in rumors of a great stone arch somewhere in the vicinity of Navajo Mountain. John Wetherill, of Oljato, Utah, related to him rumors of the arch which were prevalent among the Indians.

arxiv-1907-06421.title: Stochastic Galerkin finite volume shallow flow model: well-balanced treatment over uncertain topography
arxiv-1907-06421.creator: James Shaw, Ph.D, Georges Kesserwani, Ph.D
arxiv-1907-06421.description: Abstract Stochastic Galerkin methods can quantify uncertainty at a fraction of the computational expense of conventional Monte Carlo techniques, but such methods have rarely been studied for modelling shallow water flows. Existing stochastic shallow flow models are not well-balanced and their assessment has been limited to stochastic flows with smooth probability distributions.

arxiv-2003-13126.title: Testing Conditional Independence via Quantile Regression Based Partial Copulas
arxiv-2003-13126.creator: Lasse Petersen lp@math.ku.dk, Niels Richard Hansen niels.r.hansen@math.ku.dk
arxiv-2003-13126.description: Abstract The partial copula provides a method for describing the dependence between two random variables X X and Y Y conditional on a third random vector Z Z in terms of nonparametric residuals U 1 U_{1} and U 2 U_{2} .

arxiv-2104-07323.title: Internet of quantum blockchains: security modeling and dynamic resource pricing for stable digital currency
arxiv-2104-07323.description: Abstract Internet of quantum blockchains (IoB) will be the future Internet. In this paper, we make two new contributions to IoB: developing a block based quantum channel networking technology to handle its security modeling in face of the quantum supremacy and establishing IoB based FinTech platform model with dynamic pricing for stable digital currency.

arxiv-2108-05541.title: Universal scaling limits of the symplectic elliptic Ginibre ensemble Thanks: The authors are grateful to the DFG-NRF International Research Training Group IRTG 2235 supporting the Bielefeld-Seoul graduate exchange programme. Furthermore, Sung-Soo Byun was partially supported by Samsung Science and T
arxiv-2108-05541.creator: Sung-Soo Byun, Markus Ebke
arxiv-2108-05541.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sung-Soo Byun, Markus Ebke. We consider the eigenvalues of symplectic elliptic Ginibre matrices which are known to form a Pfaffian point process whose correlation kernel can be expressed in terms of the skew-orthogonal Hermite polynomials. We derive the scaling limits and the convergence rates of the correlation functions at the real bulk/edge of the spectrum, which in particular establishes the local universality at strong non-Hermiticity.

arxiv-2206-09665.title: Dual unitary circuits in random geometries
arxiv-2206-09665.creator: Yusuf Kasim & Tomaž Prosen
arxiv-2206-09665.description: Abstract Recently introduced dual unitary brickwork circuits have been recognised as paradigmatic exactly solvable quantum chaotic many-body systems with tunable degree of ergodicity and mixing. Here we show that regularity of the circuit lattice is not crucial for exact solvability.

arxiv-2208-03845.title: Pion inspired by QCD: Nakanishi and Light-Front Integral Representations
arxiv-2208-03845.creator: R. M. Moita, J. P. B. C. de Melo, T. Frederico, W. de Paula
arxiv-2208-03845.description: Abstract The pion structure in Minkowski space is explored using the Nakanishi integral representation. A general framework is developed for the pion Bethe-Salpeter amplitude based on the Källen-Lehmann representation of the dressed quarks with an ansatz for the pseudo-scalar π − q ​ q ¯ \pi-q\bar{q} vertex fulfilling the axial Ward-Takahashi identity.

arxiv-2304-04908.title: Representations of Drinfeld Doubles of Radford Hopf algebras Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification . 16T99, 16E99, 16G70
arxiv-2304-04908.creator: Hua Sun, Hui-Xiang Chen
arxiv-2304-04908.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hua Sun, Hui-Xiang Chen. In this article, we investigate the representations of the Drinfeld doubles D ​ ( R m ​ n ​ ( q ) ) D(R_{mn}(q)) of the Radford Hopf algebras R m ​ n ​ ( q ) R_{mn}(q) over an algebraically closed field 𝕜 \Bbbk , where m > 1 m>1 and n > 1 n>1 are integers and q ∈ 𝕜 q\in\Bbbk is a root of unity of order n n .

arxiv-2305-15572.title: The Behavior and Convergence of Local Bayesian Optimization
arxiv-2305-15572.creator: Kaiwen Wu, Kyurae Kim, Roman Garnett, Jacob R. Gardner
arxiv-2305-15572.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kaiwen Wu, Kyurae Kim, Roman Garnett, Jacob R. Gardner. A recent development in Bayesian optimization is the use of local optimization strategies, which can deliver strong empirical performance on high-dimensional problems compared to traditional global strategies. The “folk wisdom” in the literature is that the focus on local optimization sidesteps the curse of dimensionality; however, little is known concretely about the expected behavior or convergence of Bayesian local optimization routines.

arxiv-2307-11075.title: Reinforcement Learning for Photonic Component Design
arxiv-2307-11075.creator: Donald Witt*, Jeff Young, Lukas Chrostowski
arxiv-2307-11075.description: Abstract We present a new fab-in-the-loop reinforcement learning algorithm for the design of nano-photonic components that accounts for the imperfections present in nanofabrication processes. As a demonstration of the potential of this technique, we apply it to the design of photonic crystal grating couplers fabricated on an air clad 220 nm silicon on insulator single etch platform.

arxiv-2309-16348.title: Chaohua Dong
arxiv-2309-16348.creator: a
arxiv-2309-16348.description: Abstract To tackle difficulties for theoretical studies in situations involving nonsmooth functions, we propose a sequence of infinitely differentiable functions to approximate the nonsmooth function under consideration. A rate of approximation is established and an illustration of its application is then provided.

arxiv-2311-04960.title: Turbulently-Driven Detonation Initiation in Electron-Degenerate Matter with Helium Journal: ApJ FLASH 4.0.1 ( Fryxell et al. 2000 ; Dubey et al. 2014 ) , yt ( Turk et al. 2011 ) , Python programming language ( van Rossum & de Boer 1991 ) , Numpy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , IPython ( Perez & Grang
arxiv-2311-04960.creator: GABRIEL O. CASABONA, Robert T. Fisher
arxiv-2311-04960.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by GABRIEL O. CASABONA, Robert T. Fisher. Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are standardizable cosmological candles which led to the discovery of the accelerating universe. However, the physics of how white dwarfs (WDs) explode and lead to SNe Ia is still poorly understood. The initiation of the detonation front which rapidly disrupts the WD is a crucial element of the puzzle, and global 3D simulations of SNe Ia cannot resolve the requisite length scales to capture detonation initiation.

arxiv-2506-19959.title: A spectral quantum algorithm for numerical differentiation and integration
arxiv-2506-19959.creator: Jordan Cioni, Fabio Semperlotti
arxiv-2506-19959.description: Abstract This paper presents low-complexity quantum algorithms for numerical differentiation and integration in partially bounded domains. The algorithms are based on a spectral approach that allows taking advantage of the computationally efficient quantum Fourier transform algorithm. Full derivations and gate-level circuit examples are presented.

arxiv-2509-06022.title: Quantum optics in the turbulent atmosphere: Fundamental issues and applications
arxiv-2509-06022.creator: Andrii Semenov, Mykyta Klen, Illia Pechonkin
arxiv-2509-06022.description: Abstract Quantum light propagation through turbulent atmosphere has become a subject of intensive research, spanning both theoretical and experimental studies. This interest is driven by its important applications in free-space quantum communication, remote quantum sensing, and environmental monitoring. At the same time, this phenomenon itself poses an intriguing fundamental problem.

arxiv-2510-00668.title: OTFS for Joint Radar and Communication: Algorithms, Prototypes, and Experiments This research is supported by the National Research Foundation, Singapore and Infocomm Media Development Authority under its Future Communications Research Development Programme.
arxiv-2510-00668.creator: Xiaojuan Zhang, Yonghong Zeng, Francois Chin Po Shin
arxiv-2510-00668.description: Abstract We propose an Joint Radar and Communication (JRC) system that utilizes the Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) signals. The system features a fast radar sensing algorithm for detecting target range and speed by using the OTFS communication signals, and a self-interference cancellation for enhanced multi-target separation.

arxiv-2510-02213.title: MMDEW: Multipurpose Multiclass Density Estimation in the Wild
arxiv-2510-02213.creator: Villanelle O’Reilly, Jonathan Cox, Georgios Leontidis, Marc Hanheide, Petra Bosilj, James Brown
arxiv-2510-02213.description: Abstract Density map estimation can be used to estimate object counts in dense and occluded scenes where discrete counting-by-detection methods fail. We propose a multicategory counting framework that leverages a Twins pyramid vision-transformer backbone and a specialised multi-class counting head built on a state-of-the-art multiscale decoding approach.

arxiv-2511-15506.title: Impact of carrier injector design on the threshold of interband cascade lasers
arxiv-2511-15506.creator: Takuma Sato (佐藤拓磨), Borislav Petrović, Robert Weih, Fabian Hartmann, Sven Höfling, Stefan Birner, Christian Jirauschek, Thomas Grange
arxiv-2511-15506.description: Abstract We investigate theoretically how the injector region design of interband cascade lasers (ICLs) impacts the threshold carrier and current densities. The model combines a polarization-sensitive 8-band 𝐤 ⋅ 𝐩 \mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p} calculation, electrostatics, and a microscopic calculation of Auger recombination rates. The carrier-carrier scattering is included to lowest order within the non-equilibrium Green’s function formalism.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-granada.creator: Fidel Fita y Colomé
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-granada.description: Article 'Granada' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

pmc-11418815.title: Development and validation of a mitotic catastrophe-related genes prognostic model for breast cancer
pmc-11418815.creator: Shuai Wang, Haoyi Zi, Mengxuan Li, Jing Kong, Cong Fan, Yujie Bai, Jianing Sun, Ting Wang
pmc-11418815.description: BackgroundBreast cancer has become the most common malignant tumor in women worldwide. Mitotic catastrophe (MC) is a way of cell death that plays an important role in the development of tumors. However, the exact relationship between MC-related genes (MCRGs) and the development of breast cancer is still unclear, and further research is needed to elucidate this complexity.

pmc-11656608.title: Changes in essential cancer medicines and association with cancer outcomes: an observational study of 158 countries
pmc-11656608.creator: Moizza Zia Ul Haq, Camila Heredia, Adelaide Buadu, Amal Rizvi, Aine Workentin, Nav Persaud
pmc-11656608.description: BackgroundCancer is a major cause of mortality worldwide, and differences in cancer mortality rates between countries are, in part, due to differences in access to cancer care, including medicines. National essential medicines lists (NEMLs) play a role in prioritization of healthcare expenditure and access to medicines.

pmc-13214701.title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
pmc-13214701.creator: Radik Zinatullin, Alexander Sovetsky, Artem Grishin, Elena Kiseleva, Liudmila Kukhnina, Svetlana Korikova, Alexander Matveyev, Vladimir Zaitsev, Konstantin Yashin, Lev Matveev
pmc-13214701.description: Background/Objectives: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into clinical workflows raises critical questions regarding decision-making responsibility, as fully autonomous systems inevitably carry a margin of error that can be fatal in high-stakes fields like surgery. This study addresses this challenge by evaluating a “Human-in-the-Loop” (HITL) workflow, using intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for glioma detection.

pmc-13669806.creator: Jiacan Sun, Timothy J Brodribb, Ibrahim Bourbia, Eloise Foo
